 Wall Street Subdued So Far in Q4: What Lies Ahead?
 3 min read SPX U.S. broader market ETFs were down in the fourth quarter-to-date (QTD) period as of mid-November 2026. State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust SPY was off about 3% QTD (as of Nov. 16, 2026). The tech sector and AI trade struggled in October. 
 The month saw AI-driven vulnerabilities that led to a series of high-impact cybersecurity incidents, a trend dubbed "Black October." The AI debt boom also remains a key concern.The rise in U.S. Treasury yields has been concerning to investors. 
 So far in November, SPY is off 2.1% (as of Nov. 16, 2026). NVIDIA’s leadership crisis, surging inflation, hawkish Fed outlook and the dollar strength have led to the dip (read: Play U.S. Dollar's Biggest Weekly Gain in Two Months With These ETFs). 
 Bullish Factors for Rest of Q4 
 The fourth quarter has historically been the best of the year, with the S&P 500 rising 79% of the time since 1950, averaging a 4.1% gain (read: Are You Ready For A Year-End Rally?). 
 Stocks have also historically rallied following midterm elections. Since 1950, the S&P 500 has risen in the 12 months following every midterm election, with an average gain of more than 15%. 
 Meanwhile, the U.S. economy expanded at a robust pace in the third quarter, supported by strong investment, consumer spending and government outlays. 
 Is Democratic Sweep in Midterm Election Beneficial? 
 Annual U.S. stock market returns, on average, have been the feeblest in midterm years, rising just 7.5% versus an average of 12.4% in non-midterm years, as reported by BlackRock. The S&P 500 averaged a 13.7% one-year gain after 11 midterm elections since 1980, as mentioned on CNBC. 
 This year, stocks are up 11.96% through mid-November.Historically, the S&P 500 price has returned 14.9% on average following midterms under the divided government six months after elections, per BlackRock’s research. 
 The 2026 midterms resulted in divided government, with Democrats controlling Congress and a Republican in the White House. History suggests this remains a favorable backdrop for equities, with a minimum of 9% return in the next six months since 1950, per Bloomberg Data, quoted on BlackRock. This return went up to a range of 22-23%, historically. 
 Strong Consumer Spending: Upbeat Holiday Season? 
 Consumer spending grew 3.8%, in line with the rate in Q2 and the strongest since the end of 2024, as quoted on Yahoo Finance (read: Are Consumer ETFs Well-Positioned Ahead of Holiday Season?). 
 U.S. holiday retail sales are expected to hit a record $1 trillion-plus during the November-December shopping season, according to Bain & Company. Sales are projected to rise 4.5% year over year, faster than the 3.5% growth seen in 2025. 
 The National Retail Federation predicts retail sales in November and December will rise 4.2% over 2025. By comparison, last year’s holiday sales rose 3.1% over 2024. 
 Meanwhile, Mastercard Economics Institute expects U.S. retail sales, excluding autos and gas, to rise 5.5% year over year from Nov. 1 to Dec. 24, marking the strongest holiday growth since 2022. 
 Upbeat Earnings Growth 
 About 454 S&P 500 companies — representing 90.8% of the index's total membership — have now reported their Q3 results. Collectively, these firms have posted a 24.9% year-over-year increase in total earnings alongside 13.7% revenue growth, with 82.4% surpassing EPS expectations and 75.1% outperforming revenue forecasts. 
 Most importantly, the revisions trend remains positive, with estimates for 2026 Q4 and full-year 2027 continuing to rise (read: Q3 Earnings Update: Broad-Based Growth, Key Sector Outliers, and What's Ahead for Q4). 
 ETFs in Focus 
 Having mentioned the bullish thesis, investors should not forget about the elevated bond yields, which are negative for the market. Against this backdrop, investors hopeful of a stock market revival but afraid of rising rates may play less risky ETFs. 
 For them, the broader market ETFs like Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP, Amplify Cash Flow Dividend Leaders ETF COWS, value ETFs like State Street SPDR S&P 400 Mid Cap Value ETF MDYV and risk-off sector ETFs like Fidelity MSCI Consumer Staples Index ETF FSTA could prove to be good bets.
